question.worked_solution:
Let $f(x)={x}^{3}-6{x}^{2}+12x.$ The slope of the tangent at the point $x$ is equal to ${f}^{′}(x).$ Computing the derivative, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}^{′}(x) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}({x}^{3}-6{x}^{2}+12x) \\  & =3{x}^{2}-12x+12.\end{aligned}
$$

We now set ${f}^{′}(x)=0$ and solve for $x:$

$$
\begin{aligned}3{x}^{2}-12x+12 & =0 \\ {x}^{2}-4x+4 & =0 \\ (x-2)^{2} & =0 \\ x & =2.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the slope of the tangent is equal to $0$ at the point where $x=2.$
